scope: Research-only national evidence; not a calculator profile and not authorization to activate Gabon.

currency.name: Central African CFA franc
currency.note: No validated current farm-gate price series or crop enterprise cost schedule was found.

context.agroecology: Humid equatorial forest and savannah zones. Family farms produce cassava, plantain, taro, yam and vegetables; peri-urban horticulture and industrial palm oil/rubber are distinct systems. Flooding, rainfall variability, heat and water stress affect production.
context.caution: Do not mix family smallholder, peri-urban and industrial plantation data. Do not treat cereal imports, retail prices or industrial output as farm-gate evidence.

evidence.topic: 2026 cereal balance and seasonal crop conditions

observations.indicator: Cereal import share of total cereal utilization

observations_text: Cassava and plantains are the main food crops; only small quantities of maize are produced.
Cassava sowing typically occurs January-March; maize planting follows through May, with a four-to-five-month crop cycle.
Above-average rainfall in the first half of 2026 caused flooding and soil oversaturation and likely affected the secondary maize crop, planted by March for June-July harvest.
evidence.caveat: FAO balance-sheet forecasts as at 4 June 2026, not final customs data or measured harvest results. The 90 percent figure applies to cereals, not all food.

evidence.topic: Agricultural census and crop/livestock survey availability
evidence.source: Gabon Ministry of Agriculture and INSTAT Gabon

observations.indicator: EPVA agricultural households located in urban areas
EPVA agricultural households located in rural areas

observations_text: The nationwide General Agricultural Census was launched in 2019 with World Bank financial and FAO technical support; eight volumes are listed, including statistical tables and definitive module results.
INSTAT describes EPVA 2022-2023 as a specialised follow-up survey of crop, livestock and farmer-development indicators, with technical, statistical-table and complementary-module volumes.
The EPVA summary reports 54.85 percent of agricultural households in urban areas and 45.15 percent in rural areas, especially in Estuaire and Nyanga.
evidence.caveat: Original RGA/EPVA statistical tables were identified but not extracted here. Household location shares are not production or land shares. Obtain the original tables before using crop totals, yields, herd sizes or provincial breakdowns.

evidence.topic: Crop production scale, supply gaps and smallholder structure
evidence.source: World Bank Group, Gabon Country Climate and Development Report, November 2025
observations_text: The report estimates local crop production at about 800,000 tonnes, over 90 percent consisting of bananas, roots and tubers.
Cassava and plantain production is described as stagnating around 230,000 and 175,000 tonnes per year, leaving estimated annual supply gaps of 130,000 and 85,000 tonnes.
Family farms of about 1-2 hectares are described as the backbone of food production; peri-urban horticulture and industrial palm oil/rubber are separate systems.
evidence.caveat: Approximate sector synthesis, not a harmonised current-year survey. Do not derive yields using unrelated area data; RGA/EPVA tables should supersede these estimates.

evidence.topic: Food import dependence and sector constraints
evidence.reference_period: Import expenditure 2022; other indicators cited in 2025 report
evidence.source: World Bank Group, Gabon Country Climate and Development Report

observations.indicator: Food imports as share of nutritional needs
Farmers with access to good agricultural advisory services

observations.unit: kg per hectare of arable land

evidence.caveat: The XAF 450 billion amount is historical 2022 expenditure, not a current commodity price. The 60 percent nutritional-needs figure is distinct from FAO's 90 percent cereal-utilization share. Fertilizer use is contextual, not a crop recommendation.

evidence.topic: 2026 government poultry-sector support and priority value chains
evidence.source: Agence Gabonaise de Presse, ministerial agriculture review

observations.indicator: Priority value chains in announced Technical Plan for Food Systems

observations_text: The minister reported support to 150 broiler producers through chicks, veterinary products and BCEG financing.
The announced plan targets 12 value chains including cassava, pork, cattle, rice, plantain, chilli, tomato, pineapple and sweet banana.
evidence.caveat: The 150 figure describes supported producers, not national poultry-farm numbers or verified output. No unit costs, feed conversion, sale prices or gross margins are supplied.

evidence.source: World Bank Group, Gabon Country Climate and Development Report
observations_text: The report identifies rainfall variability, flooding, erosion, heat stress and changing water availability as risks to rainfed crop production and food distribution.
Fisheries are described as artisanal and industrial, with aquaculture a small share; fish potential is not the same as realised catch.
evidence.caveat: Climate scenarios are projections, not observed losses or farm-level forecasts. Fish potential is not a quota or current production target.

evidence.topic: official administrative geography for regional lookup
evidence.reference_date: DGAT source data May 2016; ministry page published January 2018
evidence.source: Gabon Ministry of Interior, Territorial Organisation
evidence.caveat: The ministry source confirms the nine-province first-level structure and its lower administrative hierarchy. The underlying DGAT counts are dated May 2016; check for subsequent legal amendments before relying on department-level boundaries. The province list is suitable for a first-level selector.

limitations: RGA/EPVA statistical tables not extracted in this record
Crop production and supply gaps are approximate historical synthesis figures

data_quality.plantain_table_reconciliation: HOLD: the Batch 50 correction file's nine province rows sum to 1,407 ha and 6,107 t, while its stated national total is 1,360 ha and 5,395 t. The original Batch 50 file also contains conflicting totals (1,094 ha and 4,778 t). Do not use plantain province or national totals in calculator mapping until the original INSTAT EPVA Volume 2 Tables 119-121 are rechecked and reconciled.
data_quality.cassava_table_reconciliation: HOLD: the nine province rows in the Batch 50 file sum to 4,287 ha and 17,374 t, compared with its stated national total of 4,438 ha and 18,035 t. Recheck original INSTAT tables and transcription before using numeric yields or production in calculator mapping.
